items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: The interviewee discusses Benny Goodman extensively in response to the interviewer mentioning the chapter title 'Foggo', but never mentions or identifies a person named 'Foggo'.

ctx.x: No, not at all. I mean you know what’s so wild? I listen to anybody in the band. For example I wrote all these things where I did a show called “Operation: Entertainment.” I had all these things follow me, a singer, a comedian, you know I had all these things I wrote for the band. And while we rehearsed a singer, and then I picked out what number would play them off, and my trumpet player, John Audino said, “Hey Terry, why don’t we play eight instead of number four.” I said, “Why?” He said, “Because eight’s in…
Excellent. When I got to about the middle of the book and I turned the page and I saw the title of the chapter Foggo, I said I know who he’s going to talk about now.

You know everybody has a Benny Goodman story but not everybody living — one of my most fun times is I used to do a lot of the jazz cruises, you know, 90 musicians would be on a cruise. And Mel Powell was on one of the cruises. And Mel Powell worked with Benny Goodman way before I did. And we sat there one night talking about Benny Goodman stories, and who else? Maybe Ken Peplowski, he worked for Benny Goodman. Whoever was there that knew Benny Goodman, and it was actually like a bunch of comedians sitting around…
